rationale: No country variable in the dictionary; the ISO3 code (CRI) is a constant assigned by the harmonizer, not derived from a raw variable.
No survey year variable exists in the dictionary; the year must be set from survey metadata.
No interview month variable is present in the dictionary.
The 'region' variable gives the planning region (6 regions), the first-level administrative division used in this survey.
'zona' codes 1=Urbana, 2=Rural, so it must be recoded to 1=urban, 0=rural.
No explicit household ID exists, so it must be built from the dwelling/questionnaire identifiers (cuestionario) plus hogar number, possibly with upm.
'linea' is the person line number within the household and serves as the within-household person identifier.
The single expansion factor 'factor' is used as the household weight.
Only one expansion factor 'factor' exists, which serves as the person weight as well.
'upm' is the primary sampling unit identifier.
The dictionary has upm (primary sampling unit), region and zona, but no explicit sampling stratum variable.
a3 gives the relationship to the head and is recoded into head, spouse, child, other relative, non-relative and domestic worker.
a4 is sex with 1=Hombre and 2=Mujer, matching the target codes directly.
a5 is age in completed years, with special codes 98 and 99 for ignored ages that must be set to missing.
a6 marital status is recoded: 1 and 2 to union, 3 and 4 to divorced or separated, 5 to widowed, 6 to single.
No question on ethnicity or race appears in the dictionary.
a8a and a8b record permanent limitations, so a person is disabled if a8a is 1-7 (0 means none).
condmig=2 (external migrant), supported by lugnac codes 2-4 (born abroad), flags international migrants, though it reflects the mother's residence at birth.
condact gives employed, open unemployed and outside labor force, and a5 is used to identify those below working age.
posiemppri gives the main job position (21 employer, 22 own account, 11/12 employee, 13 unpaid), with c12 as the raw question.
Main-job occupation (COCR 2011, 10 groups) is recoded to the IDB occupation groups; ocupfuerzatrab is an alternative.
Main-job industry (CAECR 2011) is collapsed to the IDB industry groups.
Usual weekly hours in the main job are given by hornorpri (derived from c2a1); horefepri would be effective hours.
hortotnorm is the total usual weekly hours across all jobs (hornorpri + hornorsec).
c10 gives establishment size, but its lower categories are not listed in the dictionary and must be recoded into small/medium/large.
Institutional sector of main job: codes 1 and 2 (central government, rest of public sector) indicate public sector.
There is no direct written-contract question, so contract type must be approximated from job stability (e1, estabili) and duration (e2) for employees.
Current contribution is proxied by social security deductions from salary (e10a) for employees, and by pension regime contribution (a12) and insurance type (a11) for others.
a11 insurance status (non-zero types) and a12 pension regime indicate affiliation, though a11 mixes health coverage with pension types.
The survey provides precomputed main-job income aggregates (gross/net total ipbt/ipnt), which include salary and independent income, to build monetary main labor income.

Non-monetary main-job income is the sum of in-kind salary components (food, housing, transport, vehicle, other) plus non-monetary self-employment income (ipinm/tspnm are precomputed totals that could also be used).

Secondary-job gross income total (isbt) combines secondary salary and independent income; components issb, isit, ssmb, gsi could be used instead, noting non-monetary part (inmsi, ssnm) should be excluded.
Total monetary labor income is main plus secondary monetary income (ipsmb, ipim, issb, isit), approximated by the gross labor income totals minus non-monetary parts.
Total non-monetary labor income sums main-job non-monetary income (ipinm, tspnm) and secondary-job non-monetary income (inmsi, ssnm).
Monetary non-labor income is property income (irp) plus total monetary transfers (ttm), which include pensions, remittances, and subsidies.
National pension/retirement income including aguinaldo (ttpn, from h9h1 and h9s1) is the contributory pension; foreign pensions (ttpe) could optionally be added.
Remittances correspond to money received from abroad (te, derived from h9k/h9k1/h9k2).
Imputed rent is the self-reported hypothetical monthly rent (v2b), applied for owner-occupied dwellings identified by v2a (1 or 2).
The survey provides the official poverty line value directly (lp).
The official extreme poverty line is the value of the basic food basket (cba).
a13 codes 0=no asiste and 1-8 for formal levels attended, so asiste_ci=1 when a13 is 1-8 (excluding 9 non-formal education).
escolari gives years of schooling directly; nivinst and a14 could be used to check or fill ignored values.
a15a identifies a public institution (code 1), and a13 restricts it to people currently attending.
v11 shows access to piped water (codes 1-3 yes, 0 no), and v12 can refine this by the type of supply.
v12 gives the source of drinking water (aqueduct, well, river, rain), and v11 adds the piped detail.
v15 asks about electricity in the dwelling, with 0=no electricity and 1-5 for sources; it does not ask about the main lighting source, so it is only a proxy.
v13a gives the sanitation type (sewer, septic tank, latrine, none), v13b whether it is shared, and v14a whether there is a bathroom.
v6 is the predominant floor material.
v3 is the predominant exterior wall material.
v4 is the predominant roof material.
v8 records the number of rooms used only for sleeping; the 99 'Ignorado' code should be set to missing.
v9 gives the total number of rooms (aposentos), excluding bathrooms, hallways and garage, which is the closest match to the dwelling's room count.
v2a tenure maps as 1,2 -> owned (1), 3 -> rented (0), and 4,5 (precario, cedida/prestada) -> occupied de facto (3).
v19 asks directly whether the dwelling has internet (1=yes, 0=no).
v18a records whether the dwelling has a mobile phone (1=Sí, 2=No), so recode 1 -> 1 and 2 -> 0.
The household has a computer if it owns a laptop (v18f, 3=Sí) or a desktop (v18g, 5=Sí); tablets (v18q) are not counted as computers.
v18c records refrigerator ownership (5=Sí, 6=No).
v18j records ownership of a non-work car (3=Sí, 4=No), which is the closest match to household car ownership.
